messages:
Elias: Quick QA pass on the onboarding quickstart found some copy/paste traps. Thought I'd drop them here before opening a PR.

Rina: thanks, what did you see?

Elias: three separate issues across the repo:
1) env var names inconsistent (REDWOODKEY vs REDWOOD_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_TOKEN)
2) curl/raw-header examples use the old token name while SDK snippets use REDWOOD_KEY
3) Quickstart text says 'retries enabled' which is only true for Go/Java SDKs — Node/Python are opt-in

Omar: ugh that explains a support ticket yesterday where a user copy/pasted the Dockerfile and got a 401. Can you paste examples?

Elias: sure. Bad Docker line: 
```
ENV REDWOODKEY="changeme"
```
Bad curl snippet: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
But Python quickstart shows: 
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
```
So people mix the two and get auth mismatch.

Rina: thanks. That's classic snippet drift from historical renames. Please open a PR to normalize to REDWOOD_KEY and add a short troubleshooting card listing common typos (REDWOODKEY, REDWOODKEY vs REDWOOD_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_TOKEN).

Elias: will do. Also recommend a micro-callout under Quickstart: "Note: automatic request retries vary by SDK. Java/Go include built-in retries; Node/Python require explicit middleware. See SDK retry docs."

Priya: can you add copyable examples for opting into retries in Node and Python? We get repeated tickets about "why didn't my idempotent call retry". A short snippet fixes that.

Elias: adding both. Node example: 
```
// node retry middleware example (pseudocode)
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
client.use(retryMiddleware({ retries: 3 }))
```
Python example: 
```
# python requests_retry example (pseudocode)
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
client.add_retry_strategy(max_retries=3)
```

DevDocsBot: Issue created: docs#1012 "quickstart env var parity + retry callout" and labeled docs/triage. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1012

Omar: when you open the PR, please also update CONTRIBUTING.md to state canonical env var name (REDWOOD_KEY) so future snippet generators don't reintroduce drift.

Elias: good call. I'll add a checklist item for snippet parity and run the repo scaffolder locally after merge to ensure onboarding templates are fixed.

Rina: small UX ask: include a one-line "Troubleshooting: Auth" card that lists the three common typos and a pointer to how to print the env var in shells (so users can verify). That reduces back-and-forth.

Elias: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/524 — normalizes env var names to REDWOOD_KEY across quickstarts, fixes Docker/Terraform/curl samples, inserts retry behavior callout, adds Node/Python opt-in examples, and updates CONTRIBUTING.md.

Priya: reviewed; left two tiny wording nits on the retry examples. Also requested an integration smoke test against the onboarding generator.

Omar: lgtm pending those nits. Once merged I'll backport to the onboarding generator template and regenerate a sample repo to smoke test.

Elias: CI passed, merged PR 524. Ran the scaffolder and verified a freshly generated sample-app works with REDWOOD_KEY and the Docker quickstart no longer contains the misspelled env var.

Rina: great. Closing the loop  this should cut a lot of support noise. We'll add a short note in the weekly docs sync to remind maintainers to run snippet-parity checks on generator changes.

DevDocsBot: Linked issue ONB-233 created for backporting to internal generator templates. https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ONB-233

Priya: verified locally, thanks all :raised_hands:
